description: Somos estudiantes de Astronomía y Física, apasionados por comprender los cambios de nuestro planeta. Combinamos pensamiento analítico, análisis de datos y herramientas computacionales para convertir información  compleja en visualizaciones interactivas y accesibles. Nos entusiasma aplicar la ciencia a desafíos reales y colaborar con personas creativas que aporten nuevas ideas.
summary:
Luzsi is a web tool that makes NISAR radar data easy to analyze, visualize and extract. Scientific tools are often complicated and overwhelming, while outreach alternatives are mostly illustrative and limit real scientific use.

Luzsi combines NISAR with other datasets, such as OPERA and JRC water layers, land cover and downloadable polarizations. Users can search any place, draw study areas, and follow NISAR overpasses over time. It includes a wetland classification model that anyone can replace with their own, so the tool adapts to different needs.

This tackles the challenge by turning complex radar data into something accessible without losing scientific rigor. It matters because tracking surface water and wetlands through clouds, day and night, should be open to scientists, students and decision-makers alike.
details:
What it does and how it works
Luzsi is a web map where anyone can explore what NISAR radar sees on the ground. You search for a place, draw an area or drop a point, and scrub through a timeline of NISAR passes. You can stack water layers (NISAR, OPERA and JRC), check land cover, and download the data for a spot, choosing the polarization you want. Then you press "Water model" and the app highlights where it thinks there is water. Radar sees through clouds and at night, and water looks dark to it, so the model can find it even when a normal satellite photo can't.

Benefits
You don't need to be a radar expert, or even a scientist, to get something useful out of NISAR. A short guided tour and an "About" section explain SAR and polarization in plain words, but the real data is still one click away.

Intended impact
We want NISAR data to stop feeling out of reach. Students, researchers and local decision-makers can follow wetlands and surface water over time, in places like Montería, without a specialist's toolkit.

Tools and technologies
Python, FastAPI and PyTorch on the backend (the model runs on CPU, so no special hardware). The frontend is React, TypeScript and MapLibre. Data comes from NISAR through NASA Earthdata, plus OPERA, JRC and a Sentinel-2 cloudless mosaic for context. Deployed on AWS Lightsail.

What's creative about it
Most tools are either too complex or too simplified, and we tried to sit in the middle. The wetland model isn't locked in: anyone can run their own model and connect it to the same map, so the tool grows with its users instead of being a fixed demo.

What we considered

  • Keeping things simple for newcomers without losing scientific rigor.
  • Using open, free data, so anyone can run it with a free Earthdata account.
  • Being honest about limits: our built-in model was trained on Okavango data, which is a big reason we made it replaceable
